## MARKET OVERVIEW

**1. What is the Current Market Regime?**
RISK-ON environment: Low volatility (Vol: 19.4%) with broad participation (Breadth: 6/8 sectors positive), supporting risk-taking and cyclical leadership.

**2. Which sectors are leading?**
Banking & Finance and Heavy Industry lead the rally: Banking (1W: +2.72% | 1M: -3.20%) ABOVE TREND with AKBNK (1W: +2.27% | 1M: +1.73%) ABOVE TREND and GARAN (1W: +2.21% | 1M: +1.97%) ABOVE TREND; Heavy Industry (1W: +1.95% | 1M: -4.91%) showing strength via KRDMD (1W: +8.75% | 1M: +2.90%) ABOVE TREND and ASELS (1W: +7.02% | 1M: +8.46%) ABOVE TREND.

**3. Which sectors are lagging?**
Retail & Food and Technology & Telecom lag: Retail & Food (1W: -0.91% | 1M: -3.42%) mixed-to-weak with MGROS (1W: -9.84% | 1M: -10.62%) BELOW TREND and AEFES (1W: -8.99% | 1M: -8.03%) BELOW TREND; Technology & Telecom (1W: -0.42% | 1M: -12.31%) BELOW TREND with TTKOM (1W: -3.16% | 1M: -7.65%) BELOW TREND.

## STOCK PERFORMANCE

**4. Top Performing Stocks?**
TUPRS (1W: +11.14% | 1M: +29.30%) ABOVE TREND; KRDMD (1W: +8.75% | 1M: +2.90%) ABOVE TREND; PETKM (1W: +7.43% | 1M: -5.35%) RECOVERY; BIMAS (1W: +7.36% | 1M: +4.92%) ABOVE TREND; ASELS (1W: +7.02% | 1M: +8.46%) ABOVE TREND.

**5. Worst Performing Stocks?**
MGROS (1W: -9.84% | 1M: -10.62%) BELOW TREND; AEFES (1W: -8.99% | 1M: -8.03%) BELOW TREND; SISE (1W: -6.66% | 1M: -13.76%) BELOW TREND; ENKAI (1W: -5.70% | 1M: -10.69%) BELOW TREND; CCOLA (1W: -5.08% | 1M: -6.05%) BELOW TREND.

**6. Momentum Stocks?**
Strongest 1W movers: TUPRS (1W: +11.14% | 1M: +29.30%) ABOVE TREND; KRDMD (1W: +8.75% | 1M: +2.90%) ABOVE TREND; PETKM (1W: +7.43% | 1M: -5.35%) RECOVERY; BIMAS (1W: +7.36% | 1M: +4.92%) ABOVE TREND; ASELS (1W: +7.02% | 1M: +8.46%) ABOVE TREND.

## SECTOR OUTLOOK

**7. Banking Sector Outlook?**
Banking shows broad-based strength but mixed 1M confirmation: AKBNK (1W: +2.27% | 1M: +1.73%) ABOVE TREND, GARAN (1W: +2.21% | 1M: +1.97%) ABOVE TREND, ISCTR (1W: +3.00% | 1M: -9.50%) RECOVERY—favor overweight selective core names while watching banks with weak 1M momentum.

**8. Industrial Sector Outlook?**
Heavy industry is participating in the rally but with divergence: KRDMD (1W: +8.75% | 1M: +2.90%) ABOVE TREND, ASELS (1W: +7.02% | 1M: +8.46%) ABOVE TREND, EREGL (1W: +2.28% | 1M: -10.96%) RECOVERY, ARCLK (1W: -4.07% | 1M: -4.66%) BELOW TREND—rotate to leaders and avoid structurally weak names.

**9. Energy & Chemicals Outlook?**
Energy shows leadership concentrated in majors: TUPRS (1W: +11.14% | 1M: +29.30%) ABOVE TREND and PETKM (1W: +7.43% | 1M: -5.35%) RECOVERY, while SASA (1W: -4.66% | 1M: -7.41%) BELOW TREND and SISE (1W: -6.66% | 1M: -13.76%) BELOW TREND lag—prefer large-cap integrated names and momentum trades.

## PORTFOLIO STRATEGY

**10. Portfolio Recommendation?**
Risk-ON: overweight cyclical leaders (select banks, industrials, TUPRS/TKFEN) and use gains to trim high-conviction laggards; keep modest cash to buy pullbacks and protect exposure with stop-losses on names that are BELOW TREND.

## NEXT WEEK OUTLOOK

**11. Stocks to Watch Next Week?**
TUPRS (1W: +11.14% | 1M: +29.30%) ABOVE TREND for continuation or profit-taking; TKFEN (1W: +4.47% | 1M: +59.66%) ABOVE TREND as quant leader; KCHOL (1W: +4.00% | 1M: +5.53%) ABOVE TREND for holding-level strength; BIMAS (1W: +7.36% | 1M: +4.92%) ABOVE TREND for retail resilience.

**12. Sectors to Watch Next Week?**
Construction & REIT (strong quant and TKFEN leadership), Banking & Finance (broad participation), and Energy & Chemicals (TUPRS-driven momentum) warrant monitoring for trend continuation and rotation.

**13. Key Levels & Triggers?**
Watch XU100 momentum: sustained follow-through above this week's highs would confirm the RISK-ON extension while failure to hold intraday gains or a turn below the 50-day MA (monitor technical feeds) would signal profit-taking; catalysts include CPI/FX flows, bank earnings updates and global risk sentiment.

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Low volatility and 6/8 sector breadth signal a clear RISK-ON market led by TUPRS, KRDMD, TKFEN and select banks; favor cyclical leaders and momentum names. Main risk is abrupt reversal in global risk appetite or weak earnings in lagging retail/tech names—trim positions that are BELOW TREND and scale into confirmed leaders.
